sermon.title: Adding Self-Control
sermon.series: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this short Bible morality message the speaker says self-control must be added to knowledge, morality and faith in 2 Peter 1. He contrasts secular humanism with Jesus and Bible morality, cites statistics about sexually transmitted diseases, drugs, alcohol and tobacco, and says the cure is knowledge and self-control. He reads 2 Timothy 3:1–5 on the last days and Luke 18:7 and Matthew 24:29 on God avenging his elect.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. The recording does not state the speaker’s name; the “Bible morality” theme matches Pastor Kincer’s other messages, but his name is not spoken, so Michael should confirm. This is a later session of “Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors” (the exact part is not stated; Part 6 is inferred from the order of the messages). It opens at 0:38, and the captions have no words before that. The captions garbled a few spots, marked [unclear] or corrected: the name before “said the battle for humankind’s future” (“John dumphrey,” heard in the captions; a 1983 quotation he reads from a humanist writer), the word after “teachers as,” two statistics, and “missed work” is a caption correction. He names a humanist writer from 1930 (“Charles Potter”) in the transcript only. Every statistic he gives (sexually transmitted diseases, AIDS deaths, drug overdoses, alcohol and tobacco deaths, Ebola deaths, helmet and seat belt lives saved) and his claims about humanism, a 1987 court, the Humanist Manifesto and the cost of preventable harms are his own and are not verified here. This message includes strong sensitive content: sexual morality and homosexual activists, abortion, politics and government, and a rejection of the pre-tribulation rapture view.
